old: sum: 'Thousands executed as “landlords”; the party apologised publicly in 1956; Cold War claims of huge numbers were exaggerated.',
new: sum: 'About 13,500–15,000 executed as “landlords”, by archive-based estimates; the party apologised publicly in 1956; Cold War claims of 50,000 or more were exaggerated.',
problem: Understated: the summary said “thousands executed” beside “claims were exaggerated”, which reads as a small number. Archive-based estimates are about 13,500–15,000.

old: 'Recent research in Vietnamese and Hungarian archives points to far lower numbers than claimed at the time, but still in the thousands.'
new: 'Research in Vietnamese and Hungarian archives points to about 13,500–15,000: far below some Cold War claims, and far above the lowest estimates.'
problem: Same understatement in the toll note: “still in the thousands” replaced with the archive-based range.

old: In 1972 Gareth Porter showed that the high US figures rested on misused documents and on an author presented as a former party cadre who had never been a party member; presidential speeches had repeated the “bloodbath” claim.
new: In 1972 Gareth Porter argued that the high US figures rested on misused documents and on an author wrongly presented as a former party cadre; presidential speeches had repeated the “bloodbath” claim. Archives later showed that his own low count (800–2,500) was also far too low.
problem: Our own earlier fix went too far: it said Porter “showed” the high figures were wrong, as if settled. He argued it, with good evidence on the documents, but his own estimate proved far too low.

old: toll: ['Most estimates around 4,000–5,000 executions since 1959; claims range from a few hundred to over 15,000', 'The Cuba Archive project, run by exiles, has documented about 4,000 by name; The Black Book of Communism gave 15,000–17,000. Cuba has never published a count.'],
new: toll: ['About 3,000–5,000 executions since 1959; claims range from a few hundred to 17,000', 'The Cuba Archive project, run by exiles, has documented about 3,100 firing-squad executions by name, plus about 1,300 extrajudicial killings (2025); The Black Book of Communism gave 15,000–17,000. Cuba has never published a count.'],
problem: Overstated: “most estimates around 4,000–5,000” sat above the best-documented count; Cuba Archive lists about 3,100 firing-squad executions by name (not 4,000).

old: 'General Curtis LeMay later said 20% of the population was killed; that was his own boast, not a count.'
new: 'General Curtis LeMay later guessed that about 20% of Korea’s people died from the war, hunger and cold: a rough remark, not a count.'
problem: Misdescribed quote: LeMay’s 20% remark was a rough guess covering war, hunger and exposure, not a boast about bombing alone.
area: Case file: the bombing of North Korea

old: Its officials have put the toll at about 220,000–235,000, far below outside estimates.
new: Its only figures, first given in 1999, imply about 220,000–235,000 deaths, far below outside estimates.
problem: Refined after the independent re-check: the official figure comes from 1999 statements, not a full count.

old: In context he also called religion “the sigh of the oppressed creature”: comfort for real suffering, which he wanted to end.
new: In context he also called religion “the sigh of the oppressed creature”: a comfort for real suffering, but an illusion he wanted to make unneeded by ending that suffering.
problem: Missing context: the myth-buster left out that Marx also called for abolishing religion as an illusion.

old: Cuba reports infant mortality near rich-country levels; how those figures are counted is disputed.
new: Cuba long reported infant mortality near rich-country levels, but its official rate rose to 7.1 per 1,000 in 2024 and about 9.9 in 2025 (preliminary); how those figures are counted is disputed.
problem: Out of date: Cuba’s official infant mortality has risen sharply since 2023.

old: 1.1 to 1.6 million died and 22 to 30 million were persecuted.
new: Estimates of deaths run from 1.1–1.6 million (the sociologist Andrew Walder, who calls this conservative) to 2–3 million (the historian Song Yongyi); 22 to 30 million were persecuted.
problem: Overstated certainty: one scholar’s range was given as settled. Now names the source and the main higher estimate.
